issue.title: Scoped or incremental wait resolution (then scheduler event-wake) if release latency misses p50 <=5 s / p95 <=15 s

task_type_fields.proposal:
After sase-1hf, a `wait_checks` run with at least one live waiter is still O(history). On athena (sase-1hf.4 note #2) it took walk 0.53 s + filesystem view build 3.16 s + `add_many` 4.97 s ≈ 8.7 s per live tick. Expected named-agent release latency is therefore ~7-12 s (pulse → ≤2 s tick → ~6-9 s run → ≤0.5 s runner poll). The research exit criterion is p50 ≤ 5 s / p95 ≤ 15 s.

Once deployed telemetry (`wait_release_latency_s` in agent_meta.json; see the "Wait release telemetry" section of `docs/axe.md`) confirms the miss:
1. Make wait resolution scoped or incremental. Build the dependency view only for projects and names that live waiters reference, or maintain it incrementally from the completion pulse, instead of reading every agent_meta.json on each live tick. Keep the fresh-membership confirmation and the fail-closed release invariant.
2. If latency still misses, implement Phase 2 of research report `research:202610/wait_wakeup_jobs_vs_service_procs` (scheduler event-wake on the pulse instead of the 2 s routine tick).

Proposed by phase bead sase-1hf.5 (lane-split) in PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #1, item 5. Filed by the sase-1hf land agent.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: sase-1hf implemented research Phases 0 and 1 only. Phases 2 and 3 and scoped resolution were explicitly out of scope and gated on post-deploy latency data.
